The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Pokémon cards are becoming multibillion dollar market. Crypto wants to fix how they trade. Collectors are spending millions on trading cards, while blockchain startups are turning physical Pokémon cards into digital assets. The harder task is creating enough liquidity to compete with established marketplaces. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

MoneyGram expands on Solana with global crypto-to-cash service. Wallets and apps on Solana can now tap MoneyGram's global network to move between digital assets and local currencies. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Australian watchdog suspends Cryptolink, forcing 96 ATMs offline. The regulator cited missing transaction reports and the company’s failure to respond to an information request. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Ravencoin, a blockchain built from Bitcoin’s code, could roll back four days of transactions. Two mining pools controlling most of Ravencoin’s hashpower are building a replacement chain from before Friday’s first invalid block, putting deposits, withdrawals and payments made since then at risk of reversal. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Coinbase picks Abu Dhabi for its global tokenized asset push. The crypto exchange said it secured regulatory approval to offer tokenized securities from Abu Dhabi as the emirate deepens its push into onchain finance. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

When safe assets compete with risk. Lessons from the 1960s–90s for bitcoin and stocks.. Your day-ahead look for Aug. 11 2026 Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $63,947 with a -1.22% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $1,877.6 with a -1.03% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.description:
On April 4, 2025, the SEC’s Division of Corporation Finance (the Staff) published a Statement on Stablecoins clarifying that in the Staff’s view the offer and sale of certain dollar-backed stablecoins does not involve an offer and sale of securities requiring registration under the US federal securities laws (the Stablecoin Statement). The Stablecoin Statement specifically addresses stablecoins that are designed to maintain a stable value relative to the US dollar (USD) on a one-for-one basis, [...] On December 16, 2025, the FDIC issued a notice of proposed rulemaking (the Proposal) to implement Section 5 of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act). The GENIUS Act, enacted by Congress in July 2025, created a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins whereby a subsidiary of an insured depository institution could be approved to issue payment stablecoins.

Read more on Latham’s Global Fintech & Digital Assets Blog. items.title: GENIUS Act explained: What it means for crypto and digital assets
items.description: Signed into law on July 18, 2025, the historic legislation sets up a regulatory framework for USD-backed payment stablecoins and serves as a crucial first step towards broader digital asset regulatory clarity. While stablecoins are the main focus of the legislation, you’re likely to see effects across the entire digital asset ecosystem. That could mean tailwinds for crypto assets and crypto-related companies, as well as traditional financial companies that will bring their business on chain. [...] Currently, using stablecoins to trade crypto and support DeFi activities are the largest use cases, representing more than 90% of stablecoin volume.5  Speed, low cost, 24/7/365 settlement, and programmability are all favorable features of stablecoins that could continue to grow under the passage of this new legislation—which means a potentially bigger addressable market beyond the crypto ecosystem. Some use cases in particular have the potential to stand out. [...] Under the GENIUS Act, issuers will be required to back stablecoins with 1:1 reserves of cash or short-term Treasurys and disclose their reserves monthly. It also grants stablecoin holders legal protections should an issuer go insolvent and sets boundaries on who can issue stablecoins.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies - Britannica
items.description:
United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework for crypto assets is in development, with implementation expected by 2026. [...] ...(Show more)

Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress made progress in 2025 toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. One measure—the GENIUS Act—was signed into law. [...] In the U.S., landmark legislation enacted in July 2025 has begun defining the roles of federal agencies in regulating stablecoins and digital commodities. Although implementation is ongoing, these laws represent a shift away from case-by-case enforcement and toward a structured national policy.

items.title: Crypto On Edge: How Nervous Markets React To Data And Geopolitics | E8 Markets Blog
items.description:
The nervous tone in crypto is being driven by a three‑way collision: US economic data, Federal Reserve expectations, and Middle East risk. When inflation or employment numbers come in softer than expected, markets briefly price in a friendlier rate outlook and crypto tends to benefit from improved risk appetite. However, geopolitics can quickly override that optimism. Strikes, sanctions, or disruptions to energy supply push oil higher and reignite inflation concerns, making traders question how [...] •6 min read

Bitcoin and major cryptocurrencies are caught in a tug‑of‑war between macro data and geopolitics, leaving markets nervous and price action erratic. Traders are leaning into shorter timeframes, tighter risk limits, and rapid position adjustments as every economic release or headline has the potential to flip sentiment in minutes.

## Markets On Edge [...] ## Conclusion

Bitcoin and major cryptocurrencies are not just reacting to price charts; they are reflecting a complex interplay of macro data, central bank expectations, and geopolitical risk. That combination breeds nervous trading, wider ranges, and more frequent sentiment shifts—but it also creates rich learning ground for traders willing to approach the market with structure and discipline.

items.title: Geopolitical Events and Crypto Price Moves
items.description:
In 2023, geopolitical instability due to the Israel-Hamas conflict raised concerns over potential oil supply disruptions. If such conflicts were to interfere with major energy routes like the Strait of Hormuz, this could increase oil prices, fueling inflation fears and prompting further central bank rate hikes. In such scenarios, crypto markets often experience volatility due to reduced liquidity and shifts in investor sentiment.

### SEC and regulatory actions [...] Following economic indicators – given the sensitivity of crypto markets to macroeconomic shifts, investors should stay informed on interest rate changes, inflation data, and currency fluctuations, all of which can redirect capital flows between traditional and digital markets. [...] The U.S. Federal Reserve’s decisions on interest rates have been a primary driver for crypto market volatility in 2023. For instance, Bitcoin prices dropped following announcements of rate hikes, as higher interest rates often strengthen the dollar and attract capital to safer assets. When bond yields rose, many investors moved away from cryptocurrencies to avoid exposure to the higher risk and volatility of the crypto market.

items.description: Geopolitics shapes the magnitude and timing of moves within a macro regime that the Fed largely controls. A Bitcoin bull market during a rate-cutting cycle will absorb geopolitical shocks and recover quickly. The same shocks hitting during a period of “higher for longer” rates land much harder and recover much more slowly. [...] The interconnection now flows in multiple directions. A Fed rate cut announcement affects Bitcoin because institutional capital models treat crypto as a risk-on asset. A peace deal in Ukraine would affect stablecoin volumes because it would reduce demand for dollar-denominated crypto in Eastern Europe. An oil supply disruption in the Strait of Hormuz affects crypto because it affects inflation expectations, which affect Fed policy, which affects institutional risk appetite, which affects crypto [...] Every missile strike, every sanctions announcement, every ceasefire rumor and territorial shift now carries a dollar sign. items.description:
On March 6, the US Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) report was also released, surprising markets with a loss of 92,000 jobs in February, compared to expectations of +58,000 jobs added.

Although the result was significantly below expectations, the slowdown in employment was not enough to meaningfully alter expectations regarding Federal Reserve rate cuts. Markets continue to price in probabilities above 90% and 77% that interest rates will remain unchanged in the March and April meetings, respectively. [...] Image 45

_Source: Data – TVC, StoneX, Tradingview_

This dynamic suggests that market focus has shifted toward traditional stable assets such as the US dollar, partly supported by rising Treasury yields. In contrast, alternative markets like Bitcoin have lagged behind, showing neither aggressive weakness nor renewed demand momentum. This highlights the current lack of prominence of the crypto market. [...] In this environment, weak confidence makes it difficult to establish sustained demand. Unless sentiment indicators show clear improvement, indecision and weakness are likely to continue defining short-term crypto price movements.
